routes.activity_name: breaking ankles on the Appian Way
routes.title: breaking ankles on the Appian Way
routes.description: A 28.5 km route from central Rome toward the Appian Way, linking the riverfront and monumental city with the old road and Caffarella landscape.
routes.completion_rule: Run the 28.5 km route from central Rome to the Appian Way and back.
routes.blurb: Leave central Rome behind and follow the city into the layered landscape of the Appian Way.

curation.vibe: A long urban-to-ancient-road run that leaves central Rome for the Appian Way, trading riverfront and monuments for cobbles, pines, and open archaeological landscape.
curation.ideal_use: A destination long run when you want Rome's history to unfold as part of the route, not as a sightseeing detour.
curation.difficulty: Moderate-to-hard: 28.5 km is the real challenge. The climbing is modest, but uneven historic surfaces and city crossings interrupt rhythm.
curation.seasonality: Best early in the morning in cooler months. Summer heat and exposed sections can make the return feel much harder.
curation.editorial_note: Start restrained. The route's payoff comes when Rome loosens into the Appian landscape; save enough legs to enjoy the long return rather than surviving it.
terrain: Park paths and mixed road surfaces
highlights: Circus Maximus and the southern city transition
Via Appia Antica and Parco della Caffarella
caveats: Historic cobbles can be awkward at running pace
Traffic and crossings break continuity leaving and re-entering central Rome
Carry water and plan shade in warm weather

curation.vibe: A long, exploratory Kyoto run that moves from the city into sustained climbing before returning.
